name: Ejuele
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Christina Riepe & Longdi Sylvanus. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Ejuele (Doka) [dbi] Language of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-025. Dallas: SIL International. 63 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 9.3 'Phonology of Northwest Plateau varieties' (pp. 18-19) gives only cursory consonant and vowel inventories, possible vowel length, non-phonemic nasalization and nominal prefixes; Appendix D (p. 40) states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features was conducted.' The 222-item Ejuele wordlist (pp. 41-52) is marked with three tone levels (e.g. ɛ̄nɔ́ 'bird', ènāk 'cow', èdɛ̀ 'fish'). The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the report. sources.note: Only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List records; no language description of any kind.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV (entries 'Doka cf. Idon-Doka-Makyali' and 10 'Ajiya / Idon, Idong, Idon-Doka-Makyali')
sources.note: Treats Doka as part of Idon-Doka-Makyali (Plateau: Northwestern group); Refs line gives only Survey: Hon et al. (2011). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. III, entry 187 'Idon-Doka-Makyali'
sources.note: 'If this is the same as Ejegha of Maikarfi, then this would be the correct name. Idon and Doka would then no longer be separate languages.' Sources: Maikarfi (2007). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and bibliography for doka1242 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: lists Decker, Riepe & Sylvanus 2022 (JLSR 2022-025) and its 2024 revision (JLSR 2024-004, 68 pp., 'with Notes on Ikulu', ref 701553), Williamson & Shimizu 1968 / Williamson 1973 BCCW, Blench 2009 E̱jegha wordlist (assigned to Idon [idc]), ElCat 2022. No grammar or phonology exists for this language.
